resources.string: None: streams use the main settings
Chosen by network when a stream starts
Starts empty: set only the values it should change.
You can keep up to %1$d profiles.
Streams that used this profile use the main settings instead. This can’t be undone.
On: when a stream starts, the network picks the profile below. Ethernet and networks without a choice use the profile in use.
Off: every stream uses the profile in use.
Also Wi-Fi that Android marks as metered, such as a phone’s hotspot.
Any Wi-Fi that isn’t a home Wi-Fi, or every Wi-Fi while no home Wi-Fi is set.
None set: every Wi-Fi counts as other Wi-Fi.
Saved on this device. Select to remove.
Location access is off: home Wi-Fi can’t be recognized, so it counts as other Wi-Fi.
Saves the name of the Wi-Fi this device is on. Android requires location access to read it.
Recognizing it when a stream starts still needs location access.

Android shows the Wi-Fi name only to apps with location access. It is used for one thing: telling your home Wi-Fi from other Wi-Fi when a stream starts. No location is read, and the Wi-Fi name stays on this device: it is never sent or logged. Without access, every Wi-Fi counts as other Wi-Fi.
No location access: every Wi-Fi counts as other Wi-Fi. You can allow it later in Android’s app settings.
Can’t read the Wi-Fi name. Check that this device is on Wi-Fi and location is on, or type the name.

When a stream starts, each value comes from the first of these that sets it: this game, this PC, the profile, then the main settings. On mobile data, Bitrate on mobile data then caps the bitrate. Changes never apply to a stream that is already running.
When a stream starts, each value comes from the first of these that sets it: this game, this PC, the profile, then the main settings. Changes never apply to a stream that is already running.
Home Wi-Fi names stay on this device and are never sent or logged.

Caps the bitrate when a stream starts on mobile data or on Wi-Fi that Android marks as metered, such as a phone’s hotspot. It caps every profile, PC and game value too. Off uses the same bitrate as on other networks.
Set only the values this profile should change. Anything not set comes from the main settings. A PC’s or a game’s own values still win over the profile.
Values you set here apply to this game on this PC only. Anything not set comes from this PC’s settings, the profile and the main settings, in that order.
Changes apply to the next stream after you save.
Your changes to these stream settings have not been saved.
Every value goes back to Not set. Save to apply.
Nothing is set here: every value comes from below.
Sets every value back to Not set.
Save before leaving. Changes apply to the next stream, never to one already running.
Adaptive refresh is on, so the stream uses Lowest latency.
The profile in use no longer exists, so the main settings apply.
The profile chosen for %1$s no longer exists, so the main settings apply.
Profile %1$s has a value this version can’t read, so the main settings apply. Open it under Profiles to fix it.
This PC’s own stream settings can’t be read, so they are skipped. Open the PC’s settings to fix them.
This game’s stream settings can’t be read, so they are skipped. Open them from the game’s menu to fix them.
Home Wi-Fi can’t be recognized without location access, so this Wi-Fi counts as other Wi-Fi.
Sets frame pacing to lowest latency. Nothing else changes.
Sets the smoothest frame pacing, which holds frames back and adds delay, and turns adaptive refresh off for this game. Bitrate is unchanged.

Sets the bitrate to 150% of the PC’s, or of the main settings’ if the PC has none, up to the host limit. Frame pacing and adaptive refresh are unchanged; on a weak connection the larger frames can add delay.
